text:
This
		others did

better than you

for centuries.

On them depended

your sense of freedom


your clean shirt

and the leisure of your reading and writing.

On
		them depends


everything

that seemed natural to you

like going to the movies

or being
	\tslightly sad.


What is natural, however, is mud,

sweat, excrement.


From there begins

the epic, which is not only

a
		mat­ter of dazzling heroes,


but also

of obscure heroes, ground beneath your steps,

page
		where words are written.


Leave words behind, try

a little

what they did,
		do,


will keep doing

so that you may be:

they,

those sunk in
		necessity


and gravitation,

those ground down by relentless suns

so
		that your bread may always be fresh,


those bound

to the iron post of monotony

so that you may
		shuffle every theme,


those maimed

by a mechanical gesture infinitely repeated


		so that you may do


whatever you please with your soul and your body.

Reduce yourself like
		them.


Taste the oven,

eat fatigue.

Enter a little, even if
		clandestinely,


into the terrible realm of those who sustain

life.

translation.title: Work
translation.editorial_note:
Translated directly from the supplied Spanish poem by Cintio Vitier. Indentation, stanza structure, and the address to the reader are retained.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
